title: "Housing Market - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

This time we will create our own dataset with fictional numbers to describe a house market. As we are going to create random data don't try to reason of the numbers.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
```

### Step 2. Create 3 differents vectors, each of length 100, as follows:
1. The first a random number from 1 to 4
2. The second a random number from 1 to 3
3. The third a random number from 10,000 to 30,000

```{r}
s1 <- sample(1:4, size = 100, replace = TRUE)
s2 <- sample(1:3, size = 100, replace = TRUE)
s3 <- sample(10000:30000, size = 100, replace = TRUE)

head(s1); head(s2); head(s3)
```

### Step 3. Let's create a DataFrame by joining the vectors by column

```{r}
housemkt <- tibble(s1, s2, s3)
head(housemkt)
```

### Step 4. Change the name of the columns to bedrs, bathrs, price_sqr_meter

```{r}
housemkt <- housemkt |> rename(bedrs = s1, bathrs = s2, price_sqr_meter = s3)
head(housemkt)
```

### Step 5. Create a one column DataFrame with the values of the 3 vectors and assign it to 'bigcolumn'

```{r}
# c() joins the vectors one after the other
bigcolumn <- tibble(value = c(s1, s2, s3))
class(bigcolumn)

bigcolumn
```

### Step 6. Oops, it seems it is going only until index 99. Is it true?

```{r}
# no: R does not keep the original positions of each vector, the tibble has 300 rows
nrow(bigcolumn)
```

### Step 7. Reindex the DataFrame so it goes from 0 to 299

```{r}
# rows are always numbered from 1 in R. If you need an explicit index column:
bigcolumn <- bigcolumn |> mutate(index = row_number() - 1, .before = value)
bigcolumn
```
